search_strategy: Cloned the repo and read source + the ticket in full first. Tried IMAP mail search (line 1465-1520) and the BookStack wiki REST API search (lines 1183-1416) early, both came back essentially empty for this task — no g8 remark lives on either surface, so that was expected, not a miss. Switched to Mattermost: first a broad keyword search for 'attachment' via the /api/v4/teams/.../posts/search endpoint (line 1867), which returned 33 hits as 400-char-truncated one-line previews across all channels — this preview is where most of the low-hanging clues (fingerprint helper, AttachmentTooLarge existing at all, count limit, filename cap) were first spotted, but it is also where the two scope-carrying fragments (s2-dario, s2-konrad) were seen and NOT registered, because they were single lines with no surrounding context. Then dumped every channel's full post history to /tmp/chat/*.txt (fixing a literal-\n encoding bug along the way), and ran roughly a dozen more rounds of `grep -n 'term1\|term2...'` for specific identifiers it already suspected existed (attachment_fingerprint, AttachmentTooLarge, size_mb, _ATTACHMENT_COUNT_LIMIT, _MAX_ATTACHMENT_FILENAME_LEN, normalize_detail, '20 mb'), each followed by `sed -n` to read the surrounding thread once a hit landed. It never once grepped for the whole-prompt/aggregate vocabulary (45, aggregate, summed, body size, prompt total), so the two threads that only carry that idea (#code-review 2025-03-14/17/18, #pipeline 2025-03-19) were never revisited even though the channel dumps sitting on disk contained them. No page comments were fetched individually (not needed here — g8 has no wiki remarks). Wrote code directly from its running inventory of confirmed decisions rather than re-deriving from a full read of any single thread.
end_reason: Full success on the ticket and on 8 of 9 hidden facts: PR #737 merged to main as cacdd60, CI green, service redeployed (transcript lines 8850-9003). The single loss (g8.r1.scope) is a pure recovery failure, not an infra or implementation problem — the agent never built a mental model that a SEPARATE whole-prompt 45MB ceiling existed alongside the per-kind 20/24MB one, so it never wrote code for it and the corresponding test fails with 'DID NOT RAISE'.
notable: The agent's Mattermost search strategy front-loaded a single 33-hit, 400-char-truncated keyword preview (line 1867) as its primary discovery mechanism; two of the five leaves needed to recover r1.scope were visible only as single orphan lines inside that preview and were never expanded (lines 1908-1909, 1912).

Its own running 'settled decisions' inventory (line 1925) is the clearest evidence of the miss: it lists fingerprint / 20MB-ceiling / count-limit / filename-cap as confirmed, with no fifth item for a whole-prompt aggregate, even though two lines of the aggregate's exchange had already scrolled past in the same tool output.

Both herring/reversal pairs (single 20MB ceiling + hook-first; detail passthrough) were correctly resolved to their reversals, and the reversals were found mostly by re-stating the herring inline rather than by fetching the original herring thread independently — this worked here because the reversal messages happen to quote the herring's content verbatim, but it means saw_herring for g8.r2.detail-passthrough-1 and g8.r1's two herrings should be read as 'seen only secondhand'.

The final code is otherwise unusually faithful to the corpus: size_mb from base64 length divided by 1024*1024, exact error message strings, fingerprint computed via a pydantic model_validator so every block (including url ones) gets one automatically, and the token estimator's fallback-to-text-price branch happens to zero out an unknown 'thinking' block correctly even though the agent never saw the leaf (say25) that states this requirement explicitly.
